Article Title: Saharanpur showdown: Why Akhilesh's 1st candidate list in UP has rattled Congress MP Imran Masood
Article Text:
Imran Masood has made back-to-back statements against SP as Akhilesh Yadav's party released the first candidate list.

The Saharanpur war

The Akhilesh-Masood equation

Elder brothers or stepbrothers?

The voter math

NEW DELHI: Congress MP Imran Masood is breathing fire at the Samajwadi Party after Akhilesh Yadav 's first candidate list for the 2027 Uttar Pradesh assembly elections. The list includes two constituencies that the Congress leader considers his political turf. The SP's decision to renominate sitting MLAs from Behat and Saharanpur, both seats sought by Congress in alliance negotiations, has turned a seat-sharing disagreement into a personal and political confrontation.Released on Tuesday night, hours after another round of seat-sharing talks between the two parties in Delhi, the five-name list features four Muslim candidates from western Uttar Pradesh and an OBC nominee from Bundelkhand. The four Muslim candidates are sitting MLAs Umar Ali Khan from Behat, Ashu Malik from Saharanpur, Nahid Hasan from Kairana and Mehboob Ali from Amroha. Jyoti Lodhi has been named from Lalitpur.The move has particularly rattled Masood, who represents Saharanpur in the Lok Sabha and is the Congress's Uttar Pradesh working president. Having won the Saharanpur parliamentary seat in 2024, Masood sees the two qssembly constituencies as important to Congress's claim to political space in the region. His sharp response has raised a pointed question: does the SP want to take on the BJP or its INDIA bloc ally?The SP renominated four sitting legislators: Umar Ali Khan from Behat, Ashu Malik from Saharanpur, Nahid Hasan from Kairana and Mehboob Ali from Amroha.The fifth candidate, Jyoti Lodhi, has been named from Lalitpur.All four Muslim candidates are from western UP, where the SP is keen to retain its traditional support base and expand its PDA (Pichhda, Dalit, Alpsankhyak) coalition.But Behat and Saharanpur make the list particularly sensitive for Masood.The Congress MP won the Saharanpur Lok Sabha seat in 2024 with 5,47,967 votes, defeating the BJP's Raghav Lakhanpal by 64,542 votes. He secured 44.57% of the vote, against the BJP candidate's 39.32%.His performance was particularly strong in the two assembly segments now at the centre of the dispute. Masood led by 44,626 votes in Saharanpur and 38,229 in Behat in the parliamentary election. Both, however, had elected SP MLAs in 2022.Umar Ali Khan won Behat with 1,34,513 votes, defeating the BJP's Naresh Saini by 37,880 votes. Ashu Malik secured Saharanpur with 1,07,007 votes, defeating the BJP's Jagpal Singh by 30,745 votes.The contrast is the main disagreement point between the allies. Congress is banking on the 2024 Lok Sabha mandate, while the SP is relying on its assembly-level victories and sitting legislators.For Akhilesh, the two seats are established SP territory. However, for Masood, they are part of the space where Congress can consolidate after his parliamentary victory.Masood and Malik were involved in a public exchange during a district development coordination and monitoring committee meeting earlier this year. After the SP announcement, Malik said he was under "no fear or pressure" and would contest the election strongly.Masood's nephew Hamza Masood was more combative. He asserted that Congress would contest all seven assembly seats in Saharanpur district, adding that his uncle's support was crucial in the region."BJP ko Saharanpur se Imran Masood hi hara sakte hain," he said.The latest confrontation is another turn in a political relationship that has changed parties, positions and equations more than once.Imran Masood left Congress and joined the SP in January 2022, ahead of the Uttar Pradesh assembly elections. But the association lasted barely nine months. After the SP did not give him or his associates a ticket, Masood quit the party in October 2022 and joined the BSP.Mayawati appointed him coordinator of the BSP's western Uttar Pradesh unit, with additional responsibility for working among Muslims in Uttarakhand. That stint, too, ended abruptly. In August 2023, the BSP expelled him, accusing him of indiscipline and anti-party activities. Masood returned to Congress in October that year.The return proved electorally significant. In 2024, Congress fielded him from Saharanpur as part of the INDIA bloc arrangement, with SP support. He defeated the BJP, giving Congress a prominent Muslim face in western UP.But the parliamentary victory did not necessarily settle the question of who would control the political space in the region.The unease has been building for months. Congress's decision to appoint Masood as Uttar Pradesh working president in October was viewed by some SP leaders as an attempt to strengthen its bargaining position in seat-sharing negotiations. The Indian Express reported that sections of the SP were uncomfortable with Masood's public criticism of Akhilesh and his demands for an early alliance decision.In August, another development added to the strain. Imran Masood's son-in-law, Shayan Masood, joined the SP, citing ideological differences with his father-in-law. Shayan subsequently criticised Masood for targeting Akhilesh instead of the BJP.The candidate announcement has now brought the personal and political tensions into the open."When you make such an announcement against me, I don't understand whether you want to fight me, the Congress, or the BJP," Masood said, questioning the SP's seriousness about the alliance.He also rejected the idea that Congress was seeking charity from the SP. "We are not beggars," he said, objecting to the party's unilateral announcement of candidates while negotiations were still underway.The public sparring quickly drew reactions from both camps, with some leaders attempting damage control and others adding fuel to the fire.SP leader ST Hasan urged restraint, describing the two parties as elder and younger brothers."We are like elder and younger brothers. We should not talk like two stepbrothers fighting over division of property," he said.SP MP SP Singh Patel, however, was less conciliatory. He dismissed Congress's electoral strength in Uttar Pradesh and said the party would only be able to win by relying on the SP."The Congress should simply accept whatever number of seats they are allocated in the alliance," he said.Masood hit back, invoking Rahul Gandhi's role in Patel's political rise. He argued that Patel was an MP because of the political impact Rahul Gandhi had created after 2019.The exchange has exposed a fundamental disagreement over the alliance's power structure. Congress wants its improved Lok Sabha performance recognised; the SP believes its much larger Assembly-level organisation should determine the terms.Strip away the personal exchanges and the five-candidate announcement points to a larger contest over political representation in western Uttar Pradesh.The region has considerable electoral significance for both parties. Saharanpur district, according to Census 2011 data, had a Muslim population of 41.9% and a Scheduled Caste population of 22.1%. These are district-wide population figures, not constituency-level voter shares, but they underline the social context in which the two parties are positioning themselves.For the SP, the PDA formula is an attempt to bring backward classes, Dalits and minorities into a broader electoral coalition. Renominating four Muslim sitting MLAs in its first list reinforces the party's commitment to that strategy.Congress, meanwhile, sees its 2024 performance as an opportunity to rebuild its own Muslim-Dalit political base, particularly in western UP. Masood's Saharanpur victory gave the party a prominent regional leader around whom it can attempt to build that presence.The competition is not limited to the two INDIA bloc partners either. The Samajik Parivartan Morcha, a new alliance between AIMIM chief Asaduddin Owaisi and Chandrashekhar Azad's Azad Samaj Party (Kanshi Ram), is another political formation seeking space among Muslim and Dalit voters.The BSP, too, remains part of the wider political equation, even as its organisational position has changed since the 2022 election.The SP has released a list of five, but the questions they have raised go well beyond Behat and Saharanpur. Who speaks for western UP's Muslim voters? How much space will Congress get within Akhilesh Yadav's PDA framework? And can two allies compete for the same electoral ground without undermining the alliance they are trying to build?For now, the SP has made its choices clear. Whether Congress accepts them, and whether the two parties can turn this confrontation into a workable seat-sharing arrangement, remains the bigger test.
Article Summary: Imran Masood has made back-to-back statements against SP as Akhilesh Yadav's party released the first candidate list. The SP's decision to renominate sitting MLAs from Behat and Saharanpur, both seats sought by Congress, has turned a seat-sharing disagreement into a personal and political confrontation.

Article Title: UP polls: SP, Congress seat talks turn into public tug-of-war; BJP calls it 'thugbandhan'
Article Text:
What triggered the rift

Congress cries foul

SP advises Congress to 'exercise patience'

BJP's sharp jibe

Inside the seat-sharing deadlock

NEW DELHI: Relations between Congress and Samajwadi Party appeared to sour after the latter jumped the gun on Tuesday and announced its first list of candidates for the upcoming Uttar Pradesh assembly elections. The list was released even as deliberations over a seat-sharing deal were still ongoing between the two parties.To make matters worse, the list included candidates on two constituencies that featured on Congress' wishlist.Congress fumed over its poll partner's decision and said the high command must decide whether seat-sharing talks with SP should continue. In a sharp rejoinder the grand-old-party also reminded SP that they are not beggars and must be treated respectfully.Samajwadi Party, on the other hand, defended the announcements and maintained that announcing candidates for seats already held by the party was “a normal and expected process” in all alliance deals.The BJP, on the other hand, seized on the developments to highlight divisions within the opposition camp months ahead of a high-stakes electoral contest.The latest round of tensions began on Tuesday night when SP chief Akhilesh Yadav issued a lengthy public message to Congress, urging the party to prioritise "winnability" over the number of seats it wanted to contest.In a social media post on X, Akhilesh also asked Congress to hold "serious discussions" on the seat-sharing deal."We propose that, by carefully considering public expectations and ground realities, we engage in serious deliberations to ensure the victory of our 'alliance' across the majority of the constituencies. Among the seats contested by us, the number of seats won should exceed the number of seats lost," he said.Moments later, Samajwadi Party declared its first list of candidates, retaining its sitting MLAs Umar Ali Khan from Behat, Ashu Malik from Saharanpur, Nahid Hasan from Kairana and Mehboob Ali from Amroha, while naming Jyoti Lodhi as its candidate from Lalitpur.Tej Narain Pandey alias Pawan Pandey was declared the party's candidate from Ayodhya in August.Behat and Saharanpur were reportedly on Congress' wishlist.The Saharanpur region is particularly significant for Congress, as the party's Uttar Pradesh working president, Imran Masood, won the Saharanpur Lok Sabha seat in the 2024 general elections.Congress has been seeking a larger share of assembly seats falling within parliamentary constituencies it won in the Lok Sabha polls. It has cited its improved performance in the 2024 general elections to strengthen its claim for a greater share of seats in the alliance.The list has started a fresh exchange of sharp remarks. Imran Masood objected to the SP's reported offer of just 26 "winnable" seats to Congress.Imran Masood expressed strong objections to the SP's decision to offer Congress just 26 "winnable" seats."Where is the alliance? If you are acting like this, then where is the alliance? Our leadership will decide what we need to do; I just don't understand it. Here you say one thing, and there something else happens," Masood told news agency IANS.Making it clear that the final call would rest with the Congress leadership, the MP said he would abide by whatever decision the party takes."This decision has to be taken by our party. What Akhilesh Ji is doing or not doing is not a big issue for me; I am bound by my party, and whatever my party says, I have to do that," Masood said."When you are holding talks on one hand and making announcements on the other, it shows that you are not serious," he added.Questioning the intention of their ally, Masood said, "I do not understand whether you want to fight me, the Congress or the BJP. It needs to be decided whether we want to fight the BJP or fight among ourselves."AICC in-charge of UP Rajendra Pal Gautam also expressed displeasure over the Samajwadi Party's decision and said this should have been avoided while seat-sharing talks were ongoing."They should have avoided that and waited (for the talks to be over). Nevertheless, this had also happened in the 2024 Lok Sabha polls, and some candidates were withdrawn as well," Gautam said."I hope everything will go in the right direction," Gautam added.Congress leader Hamza Masood, nephew of Congress MP Imran Masood, also questioned SP's approach towards its alliance partner, asking whether the SP wanted to fight Congress or BJP.Hamza alleged that SP leaders, supporters, former ministers and MPs were continuously targeting Congress leaders on social media, including Rahul Gandhi and Priyanka Gandhi, despite Congress maintaining silence and adhering to the principles of the alliance."First, they should decide whether they want to fight against us or against the BJP. If you check Twitter, their supporters, leaders, former ministers and MPs continuously target our leaders and make remarks against Rahul Gandhi and Priyanka Gandhi," Hamza told IANS."We remain silent and follow the alliance principles, and will continue to do so on Rahul Gandhi's instruction, but Saharanpur is our strong district, in 2012 our candidates fought on these two seats strongly, in 2017 our MLAs won," he added.Samajwadi Party, however, said that the it was already agreed between both the parties that there would be no compromise on seats held by each other."It was clear from the outset and known to all. Don't really know what the objection is all about," Samajwadi Party MP Rajiv Rai said.Another SP MP Ramjilal Suman said that the party said that announcing candidates for seats already held by the party was “a normal and expected process” in all alliance deals."Don't know what the brouhaha is about? The SP has merely announced candidates on seats held by the party. What's wrong with that and why so much hullabaloo?"SP MP Shiv Pal Singh Patel weighed in on the controversy and refuted Congress's claim that SP's seat tally improved due to leader of opposition in Lok Sabha Rahul Gandhi."My advice to him (Imran Masood) is to exercise patience and refrain from making such direct, provocative statements. I did not become an MP because of the Congress party; I belong to the Samajwadi Party. We contested the election under the leadership of Akhilesh Yadav, not Rahul Gandhi. Therefore, such claims should not be made. We were part of an alliance, from which the Congress party also benefited," Patel said."Let’s be direct: how many of your candidates won? Out of 17 candidates, 6 of yours won--that’s 30%--whereas 37 of our candidates won out of 63, which is about 70%. You can do the math yourself; so, please don’t claim that we won because of them," he added.Samajwadi Party MP Awadhesh Prasad, however, refuted speculation over the seat-sharing talks, saying that nothing of the sort was discussed in Tuesday's meeting and dismissing reports of discord between the alliance partners."Nothing of the sort was discussed in yesterday’s meeting. These are just baseless rumours, mere talk in the air. It would be best not to pay any heed to such talk. These are just rumours, and rumours simply vanish into thin air,” Prasad told ANI.Reiterating that the coalition remains united around the core objective of ousting the ruling Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP), he added, “There has been no such statement. Instead of focusing on such baseless rumours, consider what is actually significant: the decision to remove the BJP from power has been finalised. It is a settled matter that, under the leadership of Akhilesh Yadav, a good government will be formed in Uttar Pradesh. ”Outlining the progress of the seat-by-seat review, Prasad noted that further rounds of discussions would follow as the entire discussion could not be concluded. He added that the matters raised were discussed constructively.“The matters raised during the meeting were discussed constructively and in a cordial atmosphere. The core objective is to defeat the BJP at any cost and, in its place, make Akhilesh ji the Chief Minister of Uttar Pradesh. To this end, seat-by-seat discussions took place, though the entire discussion could not be concluded," Prasad said.Meanwhile, BJP took a jibe at the opposition and sought to highlight that all was not well in the opposition camp."They should perhaps focus on their own seat-sharing numbers—whether the Samajwadi Party is offering them 5 seats or 26," BJP leader Sudhanshu Trivedi said at a press conference."Akhilesh Yadav began his campaign from Raebareli. Then, the SP announced they would provide 26 seats, but following this they released a list of five names without any consultation—three of which could prove quite problematic for the Congress party. In doing so, they have clearly signalled their priorities," he added.Reacting to the seat-sharing talks between SP and Congress, the deputy chief minister said whether the deal cooks up or not makes no difference to BJP."SP has shown Congress its standing; now let Congress show SP its standing. Whether their deal cooks up or not, it makes no difference to us.""Such theatrics keep happening between the two parties (SP and Congress), but it will have no impact on the BJP's health," he added.The deputy chief minister said the people of Uttar Pradesh were politically aware and would stand “firmly behind the BJP”."That is not an alliance but a 'thugbandhan (alliance of deceivers)’ of goons, criminals, corrupt people and rioters. Its condition is neither good today nor is it going to improve in the future," Maurya said."Voting for the Samajwadi Party is like inviting trouble, while voting for the Congress would once again push the country towards decline. People are standing strongly with the BJP, and the party will form the government in Uttar Pradesh for the third time with a massive majority," he said.Reportedly, the first round of talks, which ended on Tuesday at Congress veteran Pramod Tiwari's Delhi residence, remained inconclusive.Congress is demanding 120 constituencies, including the Gandhi family's traditional strongholds of Amethi and Raebareli, and is unwilling to settle for fewer seats, news agency ANI reported, citing party sources.Congress conveyed its demand during a meeting with SP leaders in Delhi, where it submitted a list of 120 constituencies it wants to contest, sources told ANI.Meanwhile, Akhilesh has called for mutual understanding between the alliance partners and said candidates should be selected based on their electoral prospects. He also emphasised the need for consensus candidates representing the PDA (Pichhda, Dalit, Alpsankhyak) framework on every seat to take on BJP.SP has also sought details about Congress's prospective candidates and their electoral prospects in other constituencies claimed by the party.
Article Summary: Congress fumed over its poll partner's decision and said the high command must decide whether seat-sharing talks with SP should continue. Samajwadi Party defended the announcements and maintained that announcing candidates for seats already held by the party was “a normal and expected process” in all alliance deals.

Article Title: India wins Visitors' Lion for best national pavilion at Venice Art Biennale
Article Text:
India's national pavilion received the Visitors' Lion for Best National Participation at the Venice Art Biennale

NEW DELHI: India's national pavilion has won the Visitors' Lion for Best National Participation at the 61st Venice Art Biennale, marking a major international recognition for the country's contemporary art scene.The award was decided through votes cast by visitors from across the world, rather than by a traditional jury.Union minister for culture and tourism Gajendra Singh Shekhawat announced the achievement in a post on X on Wednesday, calling it a "moment of immense pride".He said the recognition reflected India's growing cultural influence and the international appeal of its artistic heritage."Under the visionary leadership of Hon'ble PM Shri Narendra Modi Ji, India's cultural and artistic heritage is receiving renewed global recognition, while contemporary Indian creativity is finding its rightful place on the world stage," Shekhawat said.The minister said India's national pavilion, titled 'Geographies of Distance: Remembering Home', was presented by the ministry of culture in collaboration with the Nita Mukesh Ambani cultural centre (NMACC) and serendipity arts.The pavilion showcased the works of five Indian artists, Alwar Balasubramaniam, Ranjani Shettar, Sumakshi Singh, Skarma Sonam Tashi and Asim Waqif.Shekhawat described the award as a testament to the talent of Indian artists and the vibrancy of the country's contemporary art scene.He said the recognition celebrated how India's traditional artistic heritage could find contemporary expression and resonate with audiences across the world.The recognition is particularly significant as India returned to the Venice Art Biennale after a gap of seven years, having last participated in 2019.The 61st edition, titled 'In Minor Keys', brought together 100 national participations and attracted over 7 lakh visitors.Shekhawat concluded his post with the slogan "Vikas Bhi, Virasat Bhi", saying the honour would inspire future generations of Indian artists to engage with the world with greater confidence and creativity.
Article Summary: India's national pavilion has won the Visitors' Lion for Best National Participation at the 61st Venice Art Biennale. The award was decided through votes cast by visitors from across the world, rather than by a traditional jury. Union minister for culture and tourism Gajendra Singh Shekhawat called it a "moment of immense pride"

NEW DELHI: Tensions between the "UP ke do ladke" appear to be spilling into the open, with UP Congress working president Imran Masood making his displeasure clear after Samajwadi Party announced its first list of candidates for upcoming Uttar Pradesh assembly elections."Are we beggars?" Congress MP Masood asked, expressing his strong objection over Akhilesh Yadav 's decision to offer Congress just 26 "winnable" seats even as seat-sharing negotiations between the two INDIA bloc allies remain under way.The sharp reaction from Masood comes at a time when Congress and Samajwadi Party are still trying to work out an alliance for the upcoming polls. The SP's announcement of its first list of five candidates, largely from western Uttar Pradesh, appears to have added friction to the already delicate negotiations."Where is the alliance? If you are acting like this, then where is the alliance? Our leadership will decide what we need to do; I just don't understand it. Here you say one thing, and there something else happens," Masood told news agency IANS.Making it clear that the final call would rest with the Congress leadership, the MP said he would abide by whatever decision the party takes."This decision has to be taken by our party. What Akhilesh Ji is doing or not doing is not a big issue for me; I am bound by my party, and whatever my party says, I have to do that," he said.Referring to the upcoming visits of senior Congress leaders Rahul and Priyanka Gandhi, Masood said party workers would abide by the directions issued by the leadership."Rahul Gandhi will come, Priyanka Gandhi will come, and whatever instructions our leadership gives us, we have to follow them. SP's announcement makes no difference to us. However, it must definitely be decided whether the fight is against the BJP or against the Congress," he said.The immediate flashpoint is the SP's reported offer of 26 "winnable" constituencies to the Congress, against the latter's reported demand for around 130 seats. Masood said the Congress had not even formally demanded seats from its ally before the SP announced its offer."I don't understand it. It's beyond my understanding; the party has to take a decision on this, I don't understand. Are we beggars? Will you treat us like this- that we aren't even asking you for seats and you declared 26 seats? We didn't even demand seats from you. So if this is your way of working, that you will dictate terms, then a self-respecting person like me does not understand these things," he said.Taking a direct swipe at the SP leadership, Masood added, "You don't care about the alliance anyway. You are just running your own party, so go ahead and run your party- we aren't stopping or doing anything to you."Meanwhile, Congress leader Udit Raj said, "A great deal of permutation and combination is required in Uttar Pradesh; factors like political chemistry, winnability, and the choice of candidates will all be taken into account."The outburst follows a 3.5-hour meeting between the two parties in New Delhi on Tuesday as negotiations over seat-sharing for the 2027 Uttar Pradesh assembly elections continued. While both sides claimed progress, no breakthrough was announced.Meanwhile, SP has maintained that winnability would be the key factor in deciding the seat-sharing arrangement.After announcing its first list, Akhilesh Yadav said the party had offered Congress 26 constituencies it considered winnable and indicated that discussions would continue."The winning start has been made with the first ‘26 seats’. Working together wisely, things will move forward." he posted in Hindi on X.Congress has sought 120 seats in the upcoming polls during seat-sharing talks with Samajwadi Party and is "unwilling to settle for fewer", party sources told news agency ANI.Congress submitted a list of 120 constituencies during a meeting with SP leaders in Delhi. The list reportedly includes two seats in Saharanpur, where the SP has already announced candidates, as well as constituencies in Rae Bareli and Amethi, some of which have sitting SP MLAs.Samajwadi Party MP Awadhesh Prasad on Wednesday dismissed reports of discord with the Congress over seat-sharing talks, calling them "baseless rumours".His remarks came after Congress MP Imran Masood said an alliance partner was not a beggar amid discussions over seat-sharing.Prasad said no such issue was discussed during Tuesday's meeting and asserted that the alliance remained united in its objective of defeating the ruling-BJP."There has been no such statement. Instead of focusing on such baseless rumours, consider what is actually significant: the decision to remove the BJP from power has been finalised," he told ANI.
Article Summary: Congress working president Imran Masood makes his displeasure clear after Samajwadi Party announced its first list of candidates for upcoming Uttar Pradesh assembly elections. Masood expresses his strong objection over Akhilesh Yadav's decision to offer Congress just 26 "winnable" seats.

Article Title: Anant Ambani's Vantara airlifts seven-week-old elephant calf Raja from Assam for treatment
Article Text:
A difficult beginning

Seven weeks of care at home

Why hospitalisation can no longer wait

Klebsiella pneumoniae

The journey

What awaits Raja at Vantara

A seven-week-old elephant calf who has fought for survival since birth is being flown more than 2,500 km across the country for emergency treatment. Raja, an Asian elephant calf, is being airlifted from Pohumara in Assam to Vantara in Jamnagar, Gujarat, where he will receive intensive hospital care. For the past seven weeks, a veterinary team from Vantara has been treating him at his owner’s home. However, his condition has now deteriorated to a point where hospitalisation offers the only real chance of recovery. With the calf too young and fragile to survive a road journey of over 2,500 km, an airlift was the only viable option.Moved by Raja's plight, Anant Ambani , Founder of Vantara, stepped in to facilitate the emergency airlift and ensure the calf could reach specialised medical care in time. This marks the third such airlift in India supported by him, reflecting his continued efforts to help animals in need of urgent veterinary intervention."Raja came into this world with a broken leg, but not a broken spirit. For seven weeks, he has fought with a courage far bigger than his tiny body. Now it is our turn to carry him. With Anant Ambani's compassion and support, a journey that would take days by road will take just hours by air, and at Vantara we will give him every chance to stand, to walk, and one day to run." Vivaan Karani, CEO, Vantara.Raja was born on 2 October 2026 at Gogamukh, Assam. His mother, only 11 years old herself, was young and inexperienced. Frightened and anxious after the birth, she kicked her newborn, and Raja suffered a complete fracture of his right femur, the large thigh bone of his hind leg, on his very first day.At an age when a calf should be taking his first wobbly steps beside his mother, Raja could not stand or bear weight on his legs. He also could not receive his mother's colostrum or milk, the first nourishment that gives a newborn elephant immunity and strength.Recognising that the calf needed specialised care, Raja’s owner and caregivers reached out to Vantara for help. The organisation’s Rapid Response Team arrived on October 8, 2026.X-rays revealed a complete overriding fracture, a serious injury in which the broken ends of the bone slide past each other and fall out of alignment. The team stabilised Raja’s leg with a plaster cast and supportive bandaging, and used a sling to help him stand while keeping weight off the injured limb. He was also put on a specially formulated milk replacement, with feeding bottles provided and his caregivers trained on how to feed him.On October 10, Raja was shifted to his owner’s residence in Pohumara, where the Vantara team has since continued his treatment, nursing and round-the-clock monitoring. A hydrotherapy pond was also built near his resting area, allowing him to move and build strength without putting weight on the fracture.Without his mother's milk and unable to move freely, Raja has faced one complication after another. He developed diarrhoea, and laboratory tests found abacterial infection. He has had recurrent episodes of low blood sugar. Blood tests showed raised liver markers, pointing to stress on his liver. Long hours lying down have caused pressure sores on his head, and he also has an umbilical hernia and generalised weakness.The team has treated each of these with targeted antibiotics, intravenous fluids, liver support, vitamins and minerals, probiotics, wound care and careful nutrition. But Raja's condition remains serious. He now needs what can only be provided in a fully equipped hospital: advanced diagnostics, continuous monitoring, specialist orthopaedic care, and a structured nutrition and rehabilitation programme.Raja is departing today on a specially arranged flight from Guwahati to Jamnagar, a journey of about four hours. He is travelling in a crate designed especially for him, sized to his small body and built to keep his fractured leg stable and supported, lined with deep, soft bedding to cushion him and protect his pressure sores through take off, flight and landing. A dedicated team of Vantara veterinarians, paravets and caregivers is staying by his side for the entire journey, continuously monitoring his heart rate, breathing, temperature, hydration and blood glucose, with fluids, medication and milk feeds ready on board. Moving him by air means hours instead of days in transit, reducing stress and risk for a calf whose body has very little reserve.On arrival, Raja will be admitted to Vantara's elephant hospital, where veterinarians will carry out a full diagnostic assessment and continue pain management, medication, mobility therapy and nutritional rehabilitation. Given the nature of his injury, he is expected to need lifelong veterinary care and monitoring, and Vantara is committed to providing it. It is heartening to see Anant Ambani support the rescue of a critically ill baby elephant, enabling the calf to be airlifted to Vantara for specialised treatment and a chance at recovery.
Article Summary: Raja, an Asian elephant calf, is being airlifted from Pohumara in Assam to Vantara in Jamnagar, Gujarat. He suffered a complete fracture of his right femur, the large thigh bone of his hind leg, on his very first day. Raja's condition has deteriorated to a point where hospitalisation offers the only real chance of recovery.

Article Title: Rajiv Gandhi's security withdrawn to get him killed, says Rahul
Article Text:
Following the assassination, the PV Narasimha Rao government amended the Act, extending protection to former PMs and their immediate family members for five years after leaving office.

Act passed by Rajiv government offered SPG cover only to PM, not former PMs

NEW DELHI: Congress politician Rahul Gandhi said the security of his father, Rajiv Gandhi , was removed deliberately to get him killed, making a sensational charge years after the former PM was assassinated by a suicide bomber in Tamil Nadu.In a video interaction with his mother Sonia Gandhi and sister Priyanka Gandhi Vadra, Rahul said, "Papa's security was removed so that he got killed. Papa's security removal was not an accident. It was done on purpose so that he got killed." "An atmosphere was created for him to get killed. It was obvious what was going on. I told papa and mom, and had an argument about it with my father," he said.Rahul Tuesday posted a video featuring the family discussing Sonia Gandhi’s recently released book ‘Belonging’, in which his charge came just after his mother spoke about the lax security arrangements during Rajiv Gandhi’s visit to Bihar as leader of the opposition, where he faced stone pelting. Rahul had accompanied his father on his Bihar visit.Even though Rahul alleged there was an “intention” behind withdrawing his father’s security in 1988, the Special Protection Group Act, passed in 1988 by the then Rajiv government, restricted SPG cover strictly to the PM and not to former PMs. Thus, Rajiv lost the protection after being voted out in 1989. V P Singh replaced him as PM. When Rajiv was assassinated at a rally in Tamil Nadu on May 21, 1991, the Chandra Shekhar government was in office.Following the assassination, the PV Narasimha Rao government amended the Act, extending protection to former PMs and their immediate family members for five years after leaving office. This brought Sonia, Rahul and Priyanka under its cover. It was further amended in 1994 to prolong the duration to 10 years.Rahul also said Sonia has not written about how she was treated by some people. He said she was “humiliated, abused” in politics, adding he may talk about it someday.
Article Summary: Act passed by Rajiv government offered SPG cover only to PM, not former PMs. Rajiv lost the protection after being voted out in 1989. When Rajiv was assassinated at a rally in Tamil Nadu on May 21, 1991, the Chandra Shekhar government was in office.

NEW DELHI: After six years of separation marked by AAP's rise in Punjab, BJP and Shiromani Akali Dal on Tuesday renewed their alliance ahead of assembly polls, with home minister Amit Shah recognising the regional party as the "big brother" in the tie-up and claimant to the chief minister's chair in case NDA returns to office after a decade.Shah was joined by SAD president Sukhbir Singh Badal and BJP chief Nitin Nabin at the announcement, timed to coincide with Guru Nanak's birth anniversary, exuding confidence in their victory and the governing AAP's wipeout in the polls to be held early next year.The Akalis had broken away from NDA over the now-scrapped farm laws.The revival of the alliance after a period which saw SAD's fortunes nosedive and BJP achieve limited success in expanding its base outside its influence in urban areas brings NDA right back into the reckoning in a state where AAP and Congress were being seen as the main election contenders.BJP and SAD are banking on the revival of the social compact between the former's base among Hindus and the latter's once-formidable farmer constituency. Much will depend on whether their renewed chemistry will enthuse their traditional voters in a crowded battlefield.PM Modi, whose meeting with Badal in Parliament complex on Aug 7 was the first clear indication of the tie-up, was emphatic in his endorsement of what he called a "natural alliance"."Putting Punjab and the welfare of Punjabis first. I am extremely delighted that Shiromani Akali Dal returns to NDA family and that too on the Parkash Purab of Sri Guru Nanak Dev Ji. Ours is a natural alliance that will ensure Punjab gets pro-people governance that takes the state to new heights of progress," home minister Amit Shah said. Modi will be in Moga on Dec 8 to attend a rally to mark Parkash Singh Badal's birth anniversary. Shah said, "The alliance between BJP and SAD is not merely political; it is an emotional bond rooted in mutual trust and Punjab's history. NDA is now complete with Akali Dal's return.""A tidal wave has started today," SAD's Sukhbir Singh Badal said, claiming the alliance would bag 100 seats in the 117-member assembly.Shah was quick to emphasise the alliance's emotive symbolism of Hindu-Sikh brotherhood in the border state with a history of social tensions and spells of militancy; Nabin too described it as a "natural alliance", and Badal invoked his father's description of their ties as "nau-maas da rishta" (together like nail and flesh). Jana Sangh, BJP's political predecessor, had allied with Akalis too. Shah's announcement that SAD will be the senior partner - Badal being the obvious CM face even though no such announcement was made - despite its shrinking base, underscores BJP's recognition that its Sikh ally should lead the alliance and look like a credible contender for office.The BJP, however, is expected to contest a bigger number of seats than the 23 it used to in the alliance.Akali's 10-year stint in office, with BJP as junior partner, ended in 2017 with their massive defeat at the hands of Congress as a big chunk of its core voters revolted over the government's alleged mishandling of sacrilege incidents and issues of drug abuse and corruption, creating a fertile ground for AAP's rise and its subsequent sweep in 2022.Congress general secretary in-charge of Punjab Sachin Pilot said, "It's a compromised alliance, a desperate alliance. BJP and SAD have not revealed why they parted ways six years ago, what were the reasons that SAD and BJP left each other. Have the GoI and BJP given any assurance to the country on MSP, have they apologised for the three black farm laws, and what is the SAD view on the hundreds of protesters who died on the Delhi border in the farmers' protest? Both parties had no political space left in the state, and they have chosen to join hands. "

NEW DELHI: Samajwadi Party chief Akhilesh Yadav on Tuesday called for a consensus-based seat-sharing deal with Congress for the upcoming Uttar Pradesh assembly elections, saying both parties must prioritise winnability over the number of seats. In a public message, the SP chief asked Congress to hold "serious discussions" on the seat-sharing deal.In a lengthy social media post on X, Akhilesh said the INDIA bloc had a "historic opportunity" to defeat the "communal BJP and its narrow-minded allies" once and for all."This time, we have a historic opportunity to come together as the two secular parties and defeat the communal BJP and its narrow-minded allies once and for all, saving the country from falling into the wrong hands and being ruined," the SP chief said."We want you and us to hold serious discussions, taking public expectations and realities into account, to ensure our ‘alliance’ wins in most constituencies. Among the seats you and we contest, the number we win should exceed the number we lose. Only victory will make the division of seats respectable, because only the seats we win will bring us respect," he added.He also urged Congress to identify and send potential seats in addition to the 26 seats discussed during the seat-sharing meeting."Therefore, in addition to the 26 seats from the priority list your team provided that we have discussed today, please identify and send us all other potential seats. Then we will sit down together and assess which seats, and which candidates for those seats, are in a winning position. Based on our assessment and the mathematical equation for victory, we may also be able to tell the Congress about many winnable seats it has not even considered for some reason," Akhilesh said."Our aim is that when the senior leaders meet, the discussion should be about candidates for the ‘INDIA alliance’ in every constituency, not Congress or SP candidates. Article Title: From ghat to gallery, Banaras set for brush with art
Article Text:
Despite its noisy, crowded lanes and walls with their own artwork of paan stains, the city is more than the Instagram reels of Ganga aarti and sunset boat rides suggest.

Poll Vote & Share your view Do you think integrating ancient and contemporary art is beneficial for cultural appreciation? Yes, absolutely! Maybe, depends on execution Not really 3k+ users shared opinion today 5k+ users already voted today 3k+ users shared opinion today Share Opinion

To linger in Banaras is to linger in another era, an era which one cannot quite date by century," wrote Harvard scholar Diana L Eck in 'Banaras: City of Light'. The inaugural CII Banaras Biennale, which opens on Nov 27 and is on view till Dec 31, gives art lovers a new excuse to linger in one of India's oldest cities.Despite its noisy, crowded lanes and walls with their own artwork of paan stains, the city is more than the Instagram reels of Ganga aarti and sunset boat rides suggest. Aptly themed 'Kashi/Light; City as Sensorium', the biennale seeks to put Banaras on the cultural map, but without treating it as a mere backdrop. "The biennale is envisioned as a long-term commitment to positioning Banaras as a global capital of living culture," says Madhav Singhania, chairman of the steering committee of CII Banaras Biennale 2026. The Biennale spans visual art, textiles, craft, music, performance and scholarship, with events spread across ghats and galleries.That approach is rooted in the idea that the city's past and present need not be kept apart. At the centre of the exhibition is Bharatiya Kala Bhavan (BKB) inside the Banaras Hindu University campus, where lead curator Gayatri Sinha has chosen to place contemporary work among the museum's extensive collection of more than one lakh objects."Can we make the ancient and the contemporary conversational?" she asks.The question is the aesthetic thread that ties the biennale together. There is a more literal dhaga, too - of silk and zari. Pramod Kumar KG, who is curating the textile and craft section, is looking to connect Banaras's mastery of the loom with contemporary fashion and design.BKB's collection began with art historian Rai Krishna Das, who started collecting in 1920. Its present building was inaugurated by Jawaharlal Nehru in 1962. The main gallery houses Sinha's exhibition, 'The Cycle of Life: Samsara', which looks at life, death, livelihood and renunciation in Banaras. "If you visit Varanasi, sooner or later, this integration between life and death, between life, livelihood and renunciation, between the appropriation of a certain sensibility and the letting go of your human education becomes very important. "Sinha draws from BKB's impressive collection of terracotta sculptures, miniature paintings, textiles and coins, and makes connections with contemporary art. Terracotta heads, some nearly 2,000 years old, are shown alongside a contemporary work in the medium by Ravinder Reddy. Manu Parekh, whose artistic practice has repeatedly returned to Banaras, also features in the exhibition. An 11ft-by-11ft tapestry based on his work, woven by Karishma Swali's Chanakya School of Craft, evokes the city at night.Biennales in India have usually been led by artists, curators or foundations, but this one brings industry and cultural institutions such as the Kiran Nadar Museum of Art and Sunil Munjal's Serendipity Arts together. "This is sort of curatorially led, but industry-driven," says Tarana Sawhney, chairperson of the CII Art & Culture Committee.The intention is not simply to parachute a festival into the city and leave. "We didn't want to create a festival that just went in, kind of engaged with the city and left," Sawhney says. Skilling and textile development initiatives are part of a larger effort that will continue after visitors have gone. For Sinha, the work is ultimately about bringing objects, histories and artistic practices together without erasing their differences. In Banaras, where the old and the everyday share the same streets, that conversation is already part of the city.
Article Summary: The inaugural CII Banaras Biennale opens on Nov 27 and is on view till Dec 31. Aptly themed 'Kashi/Light; City as Sensorium', the biennale seeks to put the city on the cultural map.

Article Title: The OGs reunite: SAD gets 'bada bhai' tag in Punjab, but BJP has bigger ambitions
Article Text:
BJP, Akalis have reunited for the 2027 Punjab elections, but will nostalgia be enough?

Why SAD-BJP patched up

The hot and cold relationship of SAD and BJP.

ALSO READ:

ALSO READ:

Six years later, a very different Punjab

ALSO READ:

The bigger, bolder BJP

Can the alliance unsettle AAP?

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: Two of Punjab's oldest political allies are back together, six years after a bitter parting over the contentious farm laws. The Bharatiya Janata Party ( BJP ) and the Shiromani Akali Dal ( SAD ) on Tuesday announced the revival of their alliance for the 2027 Punjab assembly elections , reviving a partnership that once governed the state for 15 years across three terms.The reunion, announced on the Parkash Purab of Guru Nanak Dev, brings together parties whose relationship was famously described by former Punjab chief minister Parkash Singh Badal as "nau-maas da rishta", the bond between the nail and the flesh.Prime Minister Narendra Modi welcomed the development, saying the alliance would put Punjab and the welfare of Punjabis first."Ours is a natural alliance that will ensure Punjab gets pro-people governance that takes the state to new heights of progress," he said in a post on X, adding that the partnership, nurtured by Atal Bihari Vajpayee, LK Advani and Parkash Singh Badal, had "stood the test of time".Union home minister Amit Shah, who announced the reunion alongside BJP president Nitin Nabin and SAD chief Sukhbir Singh Badal, called the Akali Dal the NDA's "oldest ally" and said PM Modi had described the development by saying the "NDA is now complete".Shah also said SAD would retain its senior-partner status, adding that the "big brother" would get the chief minister's post. "Big brother will be Akali Dal. We will contest all 117 seats.Bada bhai hi chief minister hota hai (The elder brother becomes the chief minister)," the Union minister said at the joint press conference.The two parties will contest all 117 assembly seats together, although the seat-sharing arrangement is yet to be finalised.The reunion comes after months of political manoeuvring, including Sukhbir Badal's meeting with PM Modi in August and a shift in SAD's position on the Centre's delimitation proposal. It also brings together two parties whose electoral fortunes have declined sharply since their separation.However, Punjab is no longer the state in which the old alliance enjoyed its strongest run. AAP has emerged as the dominant force, Congress remains a significant contender, and the BJP and SAD have both undergone changes in their support bases and political strategies.The partnership actually predates the BJP. Its predecessor, the Bharatiya Jana Sangh, shared power with the Akalis in Punjab as far back as 1967 and 1969. The modern alliance, however, was forged in 1996, when SAD's Moga Declaration pivoted from purely Panthic politics to a broader pitch of "Punjab, Punjabi and Punjabiyat."The partnership brought together the Akalis' predominantly rural Sikh support base and the BJP's largely urban Hindu constituency. It also helped both parties build a political coalition in the aftermath of militancy in Punjab.The alliance won 93 of 117 assembly seats in 1997, with SAD securing 75 and the BJP 18. After losing power to Congress in 2002, the combine returned to office in 2007 and retained power in 2012, winning 67 and 68 seats respectively.But the emergence of AAP, coupled with public anger over incidents of sacrilege and the drug menace, weakened the alliance. In 2017, SAD was reduced to 15 seats and the BJP to three.The final rupture came in September 2020, when SAD walked out of the NDA over the Centre's three farm laws. Sukhbir Badal's wife Harsimrat Kaur Badal resigned as Union food processing industries minister on September 17, and the Akali Dal formally ended its 24-year-old electoral partnership with the BJP nine days later.The laws were repealed in November 2021, but the political damage endured.The alliance's decline is evident from its electoral record. In 2007, SAD won 48 seats and the BJP 19, taking their combined tally to 67. They improved to 68 seats in 2012, with SAD winning 56 and the BJP 12. But the numbers fell sharply thereafter. In 2017, SAD was reduced to 15 seats and the BJP to three. By the 2022 assembly elections, the two parties managed just five seats between them, with SAD winning three and the BJP two.In 2022, SAD secured 18.38% of the vote and the BJP 6.60%, while AAP swept the election with 92 seats and a 42.01% vote share.Their separate performance in the 2024 Lok Sabha elections provided another reason to reconsider the alliance. The BJP failed to win any of Punjab's 13 seats despite securing 18.56% of the vote. SAD won one seat, Bathinda, with 13.42%.Together, their vote shares added up to nearly 32%, compared with 26.30% for Congress and 26.02% for AAP.The numbers make a case for pooling their support bases, although the combined vote share does not automatically translate into transferable votes or assembly seats.For the BJP, the alliance offers access to SAD's traditional rural and Sikh support networks. For the Akali Dal, it brings back a national ally and an opportunity to rebuild its electoral machinery, which is the BJP's strong suit.Sukhbir Singh Badal described the reunion as more than an electoral arrangement."This is not just a political alliance. There is an emotional bond. As my late father used to say, Akali Dal-BJP is an inseparable, deeply bonded relationship," he said.The old partners are back again, but the state the BJP and SAD are returning to is markedly different from the one they left behind in 2020.The 2027 assembly election will be the alliance's first major state-level electoral test without Parkash Singh Badal, the five-time CM who died in April 2023. A towering figure in the Akali Dal, he was also a key bridge between the SAD and the BJP. Though Sukhbir Badal was already leading the party before his father's death, he now has to rebuild the party's standing without his political stature and influence.Another factor the alliance must keep in mind is that the farm issue has not disappeared. The repeal of the three farm laws did not automatically undo the distrust they created. Farmers' demands, including a legal guarantee for minimum support price, remain unresolved, keeping the issue politically alive in an agrarian state like Punjab. The BJP-SAD alliance will have to reckon with that trust deficit, particularly in the rural Malwa belt, which is the largest and most populous region covering major farming districts like Bathinda, Mansa, Sangrur, Patiala, Ludhiana and Muktsar.This is why the choice of Gurpurab for the reunion announcement is rich in symbolism. PM Modi had announced the repeal of the farm laws on the occasion in November 2021. The two parties have now chosen the same religious occasion to announce their political reconciliation. Whether that symbolism can translate into renewed trust among farmers is a different question.Another thing that has changed is that the Akali Dal can no longer assume that it commands the entire Panthic vote. In the 2024 Lok Sabha election, independent candidates Amritpal Singh and Sarabjeet Singh Khalsa won from Khadoor Sahib and Faridkot, respectively. Between them, they also led in 15 assembly segments.This makes the party's return to its traditional Panthic space more difficult. The SAD has tried to reconnect with its core constituency through issues of Sikh identity and historical memory. The controversy surrounding 'Satluj', a film based on activist Jaswant Singh Khalra's work documenting alleged extrajudicial killings in Punjab, offered one such opportunity. After the film was taken down from an OTT platform, Sukhbir Badal announced screenings across the state, saying young people should know about the events it depicts.Six years on its own have transformed the BJP from a junior partner that contested just 23 of Punjab's 117 assembly seats into a more assertive player. Under the old arrangement, the SAD contested 94 assembly seats and the BJP 23, largely in urban constituencies. For the Lok Sabha elections, the split was 10 seats for the Akalis and three for the BJP.Its vote share in the 2024 Lok Sabha election rose to 18.56 per cent, up from 9.63 per cent in 2019. The BJP contested all 13 seats in 2024, compared with just three under the old seat-sharing arrangement in 2019. Though it won no seats, the saffron party's vote share was higher than the SAD's 13.42 per cent. In the 2022 assembly election, the BJP had polled 6.60 per cent and won two seats.The party has also strengthened its ranks through a steady stream of defections. In April 2026, AAP Rajya Sabha MP Raghav Chadha led six other MPs into the BJP which included Sandeep Pathak, Ashok Mittal, Harbhajan Singh, Vikramjit Singh Sahney, Rajinder Gupta and Swati Maliwal. Six of these seven were Rajya Sabha members from Punjab. The exits dealt a major blow to the AAP's parliamentary strength and brought into the BJP leaders who had been closely associated with the party's Punjab strategy. Chadha and Pathak, in particular, had played key roles in the AAP's political and electoral planning.The BJP has since moved to put these former AAP leaders to work against their old party. Chadha and Harbhajan Singh have been named to its Punjab manifesto committee, while Pathak, Mittal, Sahney and other former AAP MPs have been assigned roles in the party's chargesheet committee, which will prepare its case against the Bhagwant Mann government.Earlier, in March 2024, AAP's then Jalandhar MP Sushil Kumar Rinku and Jalandhar West MLA Sheetal Angural had also joined the BJP. In November 2026, three more AAP legislators, Harmeet Singh Pathanmajra, Chetan Singh Jouramajra and Kunwar Vijay Pratap Singh, crossed over. The BJP has also inducted senior Akali leaders, including Surinder Singh Chauhan and Jaswinderpal Sohal, as well as AAP functionaries from Moga led by spokesperson Navdeep Singh Sangha.The BJP's recruitment drive has not been limited to the AAP and SAD. Its Punjab ranks also include former Congress leaders such as Sunil Jakhar, Manpreet Singh Badal, Ravneet Singh Bittu and Preneet Kaur.That changes the terms of the reunion. The BJP returns with a larger vote share, a wider organisational footprint and experienced leaders. The SAD, meanwhile, needs the alliance to recover lost ground and reconnect with rural voters. Amit Shah has announced that the BJP is okay with the junior-partner label in the alliance. It is, however, unlikely that the BJP will settle for the old seat-sharing formula.The immediate target of the alliance is the AAP government, which swept to power in 2022 with 92 seats and 42.01 per cent of the vote. Its vote share fell to 26.02 per cent in the 2024 Lok Sabha election, when it won three seats, but it remains a formidable player.The SAD-BJP reunion gives the opposition a potentially stronger combination of urban and rural networks. It could also help consolidate voters who want an alternative to the AAP government. The drug problem, in particular, is likely to be a central campaign issue.At his press conference, Amit Shah listed three priorities for a future NDA government: eliminating drugs, eliminating corruption and strengthening nationalist forces. He promised that Punjab would be "completely drug-free" by December 31, 2029. He also targeted Congress, recalling Rahul Gandhi's 2017 promise that drugs would be eliminated within one term and accusing the party of doing nothing when it was in power.The attack gives the alliance a ready-made campaign plank. But it also puts the BJP and SAD on the spot, as both parties have been part of Punjab's political establishment for decades. The voters, thus, will judge their record as well as their promises.There is another complication. The Congress remains a strong third front and could split the anti-incumbency vote. Rural Sikh voters who continue to view the BJP through the lens of the farm agitation may also be reluctant to back the reunited partners. The AAP could benefit if opposition votes remain divided.The BJP-SAD reunion also complicates the Congress's position. With an established opposition pole, the contest for voters dissatisfied with the AAP government will now intensify. Amit Shah's attack on the Congress over its record on drugs made it clear that the alliance intends to take on both the ruling party and its principal rival.The Congress can still draw on its independent support base, but it will have to navigate a more crowded opposition space, as well as its own internal factional differences.Six years after a split that left both allies on the margins, the BJP and the Shiromani Akali Dal have chosen pragmatism over past grievances to challenge AAP and Congress. The 2027 election, however, will not be a simple replay of the coalition's past victories. And tough seat-sharing talks are yet to be held.The OGs may be back together, but winning over a changed Punjab will require more than old chemistry.
Article Summary: The Bharatiya Janata Party ( BJP ) and the Shiromani Akali Dal ( SAD ) on Tuesday announced the revival of their alliance for the 2027 Punjab assembly elections. The two parties will contest all 117 assembly seats together, although the seat-sharing arrangement is yet to be finalised. The reunion comes after months of political manoeuvring.

Article Title: ‘If I were Nirav Modi, I would get a red carpet’: Saurav Das attacks Centre over UK travel block

Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) co-convener Saurav Das

Oxford visit and planned engagements

NEW DELHI: Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) co-convener Saurav Das on Tuesday accused the Centre of trying to suppress the youth-led movement by restricting its leaders' travel, curbing protests and censoring social media content, a day after he was stopped from travelling to the UK to attend an event at the University of Oxford.Addressing a press conference, Saurav alleged that the government was raising questions about discrepancies in his passport after immigration authorities prevented him from travelling to London.He claimed that the Centre, unable to find grounds to act against CJP leaders through agencies such as the Enforcement Directorate (ED) and the Central Bureau of Investigation (CBI), was questioning their citizenship, Aadhaar cards and educational qualifications."They are now raising questions about discrepancies in my passport. They cannot find anything against any of their so-called leaders and since they cannot use UAPA, ED or CBI against us, they are resorting to such petty tactics. If I were Nirav Modi or Mehul Choksi, a red carpet would have been rolled out for me instead. As you all know, I was supposed to travel to London, but unfortunately, that could not happen because of this cowardly government," he said.Taking a swipe at the government, Saurav said that had he been fugitive businessmen Nirav Modi, Vijay Mallya or Mehul Choksi, he would have received preferential treatment and been able to leave for London within hours."Had I been Nirav Modi, Vijay Mallya, or Mehul Bhai Choksi, what would have happened to me? I would have got a red carpet, I would have been taken to the airport through VIP security, I would have left for London in three-four hours," he said.Saurav also claimed that Mallya had held a secret meeting with former finance minister Arun Jaitley in Parliament in 2018, during which he disclosed his plans to travel to London before leaving the country.Saurav said he and CJP legal head Ratna Singh had been invited to speak at the Oxford Union on December 1. The visit was also expected to include engagements with students at the London School of Economics, Cambridge University, Edinburgh University and Queen Mary University."The invitation from the Oxford Union was the primary reason for my visit. Ratna was also invited. Indian students studying there wanted to understand what the CJP movement is all about. I wanted to go there and share my perspective on how such a large-scale movement evolved into a non-violent movement. There is considerable interest among Gen Z communities in several countries around the world to understand this," he said.Saurav said he had planned to speak about the movement's non-violent character and the principles of Mahatma Gandhi, Jawaharlal Nehru and B R Ambedkar."I would have talked about Gandhiji, Nehruji, Ambedkarji. I would have talked about the principles of Gandhiji, non-violence, peace, peaceful protest," he said.He questioned why the government was afraid of the movement and said the visit would have provided an opportunity to explain how a large-scale campaign could remain peaceful."I want to ask, why is this government so afraid? I would have spoken about the principles and ideals of Mahatma Gandhi and Jawaharlal Nehru. It would have been an opportunity for the world to learn how such a massive movement can remain non-violent and draw strength from the principles of peaceful resistance," Das added.Saurav alleged that the government was also preventing CJP from putting forward its views within the country, both through protests and online platforms."We were stopped from going to Jantar Mantar, we were stopped from going to Ramlila Maidan, we were stopped from keeping our point online," he said.He further alleged that Meta had deleted 60 lakh posts over the past few months and introduced filters that automatically remove content containing certain keywords."Meta has even brought a filter, where if you say a keyword in your video, or if you write something and that keyword is detected, then that post is automatically deleted," he said.Saurav also referred to the temporary deletion of Samajwadi Party chief Akhilesh Yadav's Facebook account, which has since been restored."The world is watching how the voices of young people are being suppressed. Meta has deleted 6 million posts. We are being denied the freedom to express ourselves both on the streets and online. Akhilesh Yadav's Facebook account has also been deactivated," he said."If the youth have to keep their point, where should they go?" he asked.
Article Summary: CJP co-convener Saurav Das accused the Centre of trying to suppress the youth- led movement. He was stopped from travelling to the UK to attend an event at the University of Oxford. Saurav alleged that the government was raising questions about discrepancies in his passport.

Article Title: ‘Sitting at the feet of the same BJP’: Bhagwant Mann attacks Sukhbir Badal over alliance
Article Text:
Bhagwant Mann attacks Sukhbir Badal over alliance

BJP and SAD revive alliance after six-year break

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: Punjab chief minister Bhagwant Mann on Tuesday criticised the newly announced alliance between Bharatiya Janata Party ( BJP ) and Shiromani Akali Dal (SAD) for the 2027 Assembly elections, accusing SAD president Sukhbir Singh Badal of aligning with the same party he had previously criticised over its handling of farmers' issues.In a video statement shared by the Aam Aadmi Party (AAP), Mann alleged that the Badal family had initially supported the three farm laws introduced by the Centre in 2020 but changed its stand after the farmers' protest gained momentum and widespread support.Referring to the resignation of then Union Minister of Food Processing Industries Harsimrat Kaur Badal, Mann claimed the Akali Dal had realised that it would struggle to survive politically in Punjab if it continued to support the laws."The BJP and the Akali Dal have formed an alliance. I would like to remind you of what they say to each other, how these people try to make a fool of the public. They feel that people forget things after some time. At first, the entire Badal family kept speaking in favour of these 'black laws', saying, 'That's a very good law, a very good law. It is amazing; if it does amazing work, then with this, the agriculture of Punjab will become very prosperous.' When the farmers' movement reached its peak and started getting support from all over the world, they realised this would be a mistake and that it would be difficult to survive politically in Punjab," he said."So, Harsimrat resigned and started speaking against those laws, claiming, 'The BJP is anti-farmer, the BJP is anti-farmer, we have sacrificed, the BJP is anti-farmer.' But by then, people understood that they were still in talks with each other and were separating from each other just to put on a show for the public," he added.Harsimrat Kaur Badal resigned from the Union Cabinet in September 2020, before the Lok Sabha voted on the farm bills. Days after the Rajya Sabha cleared the final bill, Sukhbir Singh Badal announced the SAD's unanimous decision to withdraw from the National Democratic Alliance (NDA).Mann also accused the BJP of neglecting Punjab's interests, citing the state's tableau at national events on Republic Day and Independence Day."The same BJP says that the tableau that comes out on January 26 or August 15 will not be Punjab's tableau in Delhi. We got this work done by fighting with them," he said.Targeting Sukhbir Badal over his earlier criticism of the BJP, Mann alleged that the SAD president had accused the party of interfering in Sikh religious institutions with the help of the Rashtriya Swayamsevak Sangh (RSS)."The same BJP about which Sukhbir Badal used to say that Sikh organisations are being taken over by the BJP with the help of the RSS, that the BJP has captured the committee of Hazur Sahib in Maharashtra and the committee of Patna Sahib. Today, sitting at the feet of that same BJP, you are making a political alliance," he said.Appealing to people to support the AAP government, Mann said, "Aam Aadmi Party is your own party. There is a party living in your hearts. I will come at your call, wherever you call me. We will come and raise our voice in favour of Punjab."Mann's remarks came after BJP and SAD announced on Tuesday that they would contest the 2027 Punjab Assembly elections together, reviving their alliance after a six-year break. The two parties will jointly contest all 117 Assembly seats, with the SAD taking the lead in the arrangement."Big brother will be Akali Dal. We will contest all 117 seats. Bada bhai hi chief minister hota hai (The elder brother becomes the chief minister)," Union Home Minister Amit Shah said at a joint press conference attended by BJP president Nitin Nabin and Sukhbir Singh Badal."Naturally, the Shiromani Akali Dal (SAD) will play the role of the elder brother. The Akali Dal and the Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) will contest together. Both parties will jointly contest all 117 seats, while the Akali Dal will be in the role of the elder brother," Shah added.The announcement, made on Gurpurab, marked the revival of ties between the two parties, which ended their partnership in 2020 after the SAD withdrew from the NDA over its opposition to the farm laws.Under their previous seat-sharing arrangement, the BJP contested 23 of Punjab's 117 Assembly seats, while the SAD fielded candidates in the remaining constituencies. The two parties had jointly governed the state for 10 years before losing the 2017 Assembly elections, when the Congress returned to power under Captain Amarinder Singh.In the 2022 Assembly elections, the AAP swept to power, while the BJP and SAD, which contested separately, were pushed to the margins.Meanwhile, the Punjab BJP on Monday announced its 16-member state election committee for the 2027 Assembly polls, with state president Kewal Singh Dhillon heading the panel.
Article Summary: BJP and SAD revive alliance after six-year break. The two parties will jointly contest all 117 Assembly seats, with the SAD taking the lead in the arrangement. Punjab chief minister Bhagwant Mann accused SAD president Sukhbir Singh Badal of aligning with the same party he had previously criticised over its handling of farmers' issues.

Article Title: Presidential election today? Trump confuses India with Brazil, claims 125 million voted
Article Text:
Trump says "125 million Indians voted in presidential election today."

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

US President Donald Trump on Monday confused India with Brazil, claiming that 125 million people had voted in an Indian “presidential election”, while also questioning the integrity of the American voting system.In a post on Truth Social, Trump wrote, “125 Million People voted today in the first round of India’s Presidential Election. The results came out shortly after the vote closed, on the same day!”He then compared the alleged election results with the US electoral process, writing, “In Detroit, Philadelphia, California, and numerous other US Cities and States, the results, with much smaller numbers, will often take weeks to Rig, I mean, calculate. Voting in America is corrupt!!!”However, India did not hold a presidential election on Sunday. The President of India is elected indirectly by an electoral college and not through a direct nationwide popular vote.Trump's remarks came after Brazil held the first round of its presidential election on Sunday, with incumbent President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva and right-wing challenger Flávio Bolsonaro advancing to the October 25 runoff.With 99.99% of the votes counted, Bolsonaro secured 47.03% of the valid votes, while Lula received 45.16%, according to Brazil's Superior Electoral Court.The figure of around 125 million mentioned by Trump is close to Brazil's total valid votes, which stood at about 125.27 million, suggesting he may have confused the Brazilian election with India.Neither Bolsonaro nor Lula crossed the 50% threshold required to win in the first round, triggering the October 25 runoff, BBC reported.Flávio Bolsonaro, the son of former Brazilian president Jair Bolsonaro, outperformed expectations in the first round and finished ahead of Lula. His strong showing has raised the prospect of a shift to the right in Latin America's largest economy.Brazil has used electronic voting for decades, and electoral authorities said the first-round voting process proceeded smoothly.The Organization of American States' electoral observation mission said “the voting has been going smoothly and under adequate safety conditions.”The rapid announcement of results has also been cited as a strength of Brazil's electronic voting system.“When results take a lot of time, it creates an opening for people to cast doubt on the results, to say there’s been a problem,” Josemar Lauriano Pereira, a 46-year-old lawyer in Rio de Janeiro, told the Associated Press.Trump's post drew reactions on social media, with users pointing out that India does not elect its president through a direct popular vote.One user posted, “Trump living in a different world? Is a presidential election taking place in India? President Donald Trump made the incorrect claim that 125 million people voted in India's "presidential election" today.”Another said, “What is my blud Donald Trump smoking? Why is he mentioning India instead of Brazil when talking about the election?”
Article Summary: US President Donald Trump confused India with Brazil, claiming that 125 million people had voted in an Indian "presidential election" He also questioned the integrity of the American voting system. India did not hold a presidential election on Sunday. The President of India is elected indirectly by an electoral college.

Article Title: A 17-year-old MP girl stopped her family from marrying her off to continue her education, sought help from teachers; now in Class 12, she dreams of becoming a teacher, with David Beckham sharing her s
Article Text:
Teen fends off child marriage, earns David Beckham praise





INDORE: When Hima Ninama's kin decided to marry her off at 17, she refused to let child marriage derail her education. The Class 11 student from Madhya Pradesh's Jhabua district turned to her teachers for help, stopped the wedding, and stayed in school.UNICEF India documented Hima's inspiring journey, which later caught global attention when international football legend and UNICEF goodwill ambassador David Beckham shared her story on social media on World Children's Day (Nov 20).When her marriage was fixed, Hima approached her teachers at Sandipani School in Kalyanpura, unwilling to bow to family pressure. Principal GP Ojha and other teachers spoke to her family, explaining the consequences of child marriage and the importance of letting her continue her education.The intervention, coupled with Hima’s resolve, helped call off the wedding.Hima later cleared her Class 11 examination in first division. Now in Class 12, she dreams of becoming a teacher and helping other girls pursue education and become self-reliant. She is also active in sports.A UNICEF India team visited her village and school and covered her journey in a short documentary. “My family wanted me to get married, but I refused.I wanted to study. I was also interested in sports, but because I cannot walk properly, I used to stay away until my teacher counselled and encouraged me to participate,” Hima said in the documentary.Sharing Hima’s story on social media, former England football captain Beckham reflected on his two decades of association with UNICEF and said he had seen how girls could lead, progress and make decisions about their lives when given the right support and opportunities.
Article Summary: Hima Ninama's family planned to marry her off at 17. She refused to bow to family pressure and asked her teachers for help. UNICEF India documented Hima's inspiring journey. David Beckham shared her story on social media on World Children's Day.

Article Title: Three years after suffering cardiac arrest during an NFL game, Damar Hamlin signs a new Under Armour partnership focused on the mental challenges young athletes face
Article Text:
Three years after suffering cardiac arrest during an NFL game, Damar Hamlin signs a new Under Armour partnership focused on the mental challenges young athletes face

Under Armour Partnership Focuses on Young Athletes' Mental Health

Hamlin's Family Background and Early Life

From College Football to the NFL

Cardiac Arrest and His Comeback
